subject: Renewal health & commit choices — Lumina usage stewardship
messages:
From: Alex Tan <alex.tan@luminahealth.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick sync — renewal runway and recent token surge

Hi Grace,

Hope you’re well. We’re starting internal renewal planning and noticed token spend jumped ~48% month-over-month in early May (mostly inference for patient summary generation at higher prompt lengths). Before we lock in a new commit, procurement asked for: 1) a short operational readout explaining the spike, 2) a latency/quality snapshot vs our current model mix, and 3) a few commit/term options that would reduce unit cost without degrading SLA.

Can you run a quick usage health recap and share what you think the right guardrails are for the next 6–12 months? No need for a full deck — a one-page summary plus a short call will do.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Tan
Head of ML Integrations — LuminaHealth
[Attachment: sample_output_example.txt (txt)]
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
To: Alex Tan <alex.tan@luminahealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick sync — renewal runway and recent token surge

Alex — thanks for the heads up. We can do that. At a high level: early-May spike looks tied to two product changes on your side (longer system prompts + increased batch sizes from a new async worker). We observed a 35% higher avg sequence length and a small increase in KV-cache misses for the larger batches which pushed token processing time up ~12ms per token for those flows.

I’m looping in Ben (CS) and Karthik (SE) — Ben can share operational logs and Karthik can run a quick latency/quality matrix across the models you’re using. Ben — attaching a raw usage extract; can you flag any abnormal retry patterns? Karthik — can you include quantization/half-precision tradeoffs that keep quality within current thresholds?

Proposed next steps:
- We’ll produce a 1-page usage health recap (incl. token breakout by route, top 5 queries by sequence length).
- Karthik will run a latency vs. model-mix snapshot (p50/p95) and a low-CPU quantized profile.
- We'll propose 2 commit options (12–month and 6–month) with burst lanes and a prefetch/caching suggestion to shave token cost.

Available to meet Thurs 20th 10–11am PT or Fri 21st 8–10am PT — which works for your team?

Cheers,
Grace O’Connor
Account Exec — Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 08:46:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Lumina health readout prep

Quick internal note — pulled logs for the 48-hour window Alex referenced. Findings:
- Retry loop visible for 2 endpoints (avg retries 1.2 on those routes) that align with the new async worker rollout.
- Cache hit rate for prefix caching dropped from 82% to 59% on the patient-summary route after the change.
- Burst traffic is concentrated between 01:00–03:00 UTC (ET overnight processing).

I attached latency bench (raw) and a token-breakdown CSV. Karthik: I recommend we test a mixed strategy — keep the higher-fidelity model for long-form summaries but route shorter requests to a trimmed variant with distilled head to save tokens. Also suggest a short-lived increased burst lane (30% capacity) for nightly ETL windows to avoid async retries.

I’ll join the customer call. Meeting confirmed for Fri 21st 09:00 PT.

Ben Carter
Customer Success — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: latency_bench_v2.csv (csv)]
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
To: Alex Tan <alex.tan@luminahealth.com>, Procurement <procurement@luminahealth.com>, J. Patel <j.patel@luminahealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick sync — renewal runway and recent token surge

Alex / team — thanks for the call this morning. Attached is the 1‑page health recap and a short set of commit options. Summary (TL;DR):

- Root cause: product rollout changed average prompt length + batching behavior causing cache erosion and retry pressure in nightly jobs.
- Impact: estimated incremental token cost ~ $9.7k/month at current run-rate; projected to normalize to ~$3.1k/month after implementing route-level caching and a 30% burst lane for ETL windows.
- Latency: p95 for long-form summary route increased from 420ms to 610ms during peak; quantized profile reduces p95 to ~460ms with negligible quality delta on our eval set.

Commit options (high level):
1) 12-month commit (best unit-price): 1.2B tokens included, 15% discount on overage, dedicated burst lane for nightly ETL. Preferable if Lumina wants predictable unit economics.
2) 6-month flex commit: 600M tokens included, 8% discount on overage, includes a one-time prefetch/caching implementation credit.
3) Short-term bridge: monthly with burst credits (useful if you expect the rewrite to land in <3 months).

Action items we agreed on:
- Redwood to deliver: health recap (attached), latency bench (attached), and redlines_summary for the 6-month option.
- Lumina to confirm preferred option and procurement contacts for PO routing by EOD Wed 26 May.
- Joint scheduling: maintenance window for cache prefill (suggest Sat 29 May 02:00–04:00 UTC).

Attachments included: usage_report_May2027.pdf, latency_bench_v2.csv, redlines_summary.docx

If Procurement needs a one-page commercial summary for their packet, we can produce that by Monday.

—Grace
Grace O’Connor
Account Exec — Redwood Inference
